title: Building a nested if, line by line
idea: Assemble a nested if from the inside out: outer question, then the inner question in its branch. Arrange and complete code with predictable output.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a nested if: check the weather, then (only if raining) check for an umbrella.
exercises.explanation: Outer if first, then the inner if indented inside its body, then the inner else matched to the inner if.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the keyword that starts the inner decision:

if raining:
    ____ have_umbrella:
        print("Take a walk")
exercises.explanation: The inner decision also starts with 'if'. It just lives one level deeper, inside the outer body.

exercises.prompt: After typing 'if raining:' what must the very next line (the inner if) have?
options: More indentation than the outer if
The same indentation as the outer if
exercises.explanation: The inner if is part of the outer body, so it must be indented further in. That extra indent is what makes it 'nested'.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: a store is open; inside, check if an item is in stock.
exercises.explanation: Outer if and its inner if/else, then the outer else lined up with the outer if to catch the closed-store case.
The inner else, indented to match the inner if, handles in_stock being False.

exercises.prompt: You wrote 'if store_open:' and want the 'Come back later' message for when it is closed. Where does that else go?
options: At the outer indent level, matching 'if store_open:'
exercises.explanation: To answer the outer if, the else must share its indentation. Then it runs only when store_open is False.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a plain-English plan for 'Can I ride? Tall enough, then old enough?'.
blocks: If tall enough, check if old enough
exercises.explanation: Plan outer-first: the height gate, then the age gate inside it. The plan maps straight onto a nested if.
tall_enough is True so we go inside; old_enough is False so the inner else runs: 'Too young'.

options: The outer if (it runs when tall_enough is False)
The inner if (it runs when old_enough is False)
exercises.explanation: That else lines up with 'if tall_enough:', so it answers the OUTER question - it runs when the rider is too short.

exercises.prompt: The safest way to build a nested if is...
options: write the outer if first, then add the inner if inside its body
write the deepest print and work outward by guessing
skip the indentation and add it later
exercises.explanation: Build outer-first: the outer decision frames where the inner one goes. Correct indentation as you type keeps the branches clear.
